doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Can intuition be taught? Specialization
summary: Jeannie and Jimmy say intuition is endowed and that post-war specialization compartmentalized people.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well you’ve both been in the education field for a while. Is there any way you can teach intuitiveness?
No. Intuitiveness I think is endowed. And I think everybody is endowed.

I would say everybody has a certain aspect of intuitiveness, depending upon how it’s utilized or exercised. Because to me, that’s part of the sensitivity that exists in all of us in terms of dealing with survival.

I’m always amazed how a person can be intuitive in this area, and completely blank right here. That always amazes me. Because to me if you’re intuitive, you’re intuitive. But again there’s a different era now, before everything became so compartmentalized. Weird.

Compartmentalized. In other words, coming into the 50s, right out of the late 40s, but especially after World War II, on up to now in terms of high tech, we entered into the age of specialists. So we divided up the human body. You’ve got an ache on your left side, you go to see a doctor who does the left ear. The right side, the doctor does the right ear. And the eyes, the same way. So you’re all divided up. And you’ve got to go through all this to find out what’s wrong.
That’s right. And you’ve got to see about six of them first before they decide which.
And in the meantime they’ve written up all these prescriptions for you, and it breaks down the rest of your body while you’re trying to take care of it. Not all of them.

So it becomes pretty wild. You know that’s why I think the basic sense again of why we go back to that education, having that foundation you see, and when you deal with the nature of what is, and then go from there. And lots of luck.
